transcript.text: Dropped a cast iron pan on my ceramic hob and there's a crack right across the front left ring. It still heats up. Can I keep using it until I get a new one?

No, please stop using it immediately as a crack creates a serious risk of electric shock or fire if moisture reaches the live components underneath. The damage is almost certainly from the impact of the heavy pan rather than normal wear or settings. To be sure there are no other issues, just check that the control panel isn't showing any error codes and that the rest of the surface feels secure with no loose shards. Once you’ve switched it off at the wall, I can help you look up a replacement part for your specific model if you have the label handy.

Ok, I won't use it. No error codes and the controls still respond. The crack runs about 20cm towards the control area, and some pasta water spilled earlier that might have gone into it. I can switch it off at the red cooker switch on the wall. I can't get to the model label though, as the oven is built in underneath.

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. The crack running towards the controls combined with water exposure makes this a definite electrical hazard that requires a qualified engineer to inspect before it can be used again. The most likely cause is physical damage from the pan, which has compromised the glass and allowed moisture into the underlying electronics. Because you cannot reach the model label right now, please look for a sticker on the frame of the hob or inside the door seal when the oven below is open. Once we have that number, I can help identify the specific part needed to make it safe.

reading.symptom: crack across the front left ring

plan: They asked: "Can I keep using it until I get a new one?" - answer that first.
The fault they reported is: "crack across the front left ring". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply.

Safety: a electrical water hazard is active. The fixed safety warning is shown separately, do not repeat it. It must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it: say that plainly. You may explain the likely cause and suggest checks that are safe with it switched off and unplugged, but never say or imply that a check could make it safe to use, or that they might not need an engineer.
Already told them (do not repeat any of it; build on it): turn 1: safety stop.
Checks they have done and what they found: checked for error codes - no error codes; tested controls - controls still respond.
The fault they reported is: "crack across the front left ring". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 2: the checks they reported did not fix it and they cannot reach the model label right now. Carry on without it: give the next check or say what the likely part is, and tell them where to find the model number later.
